messages:
alex_ross: :rotating_light: GCP eu-west2 interconnect is flapping — we're seeing high packet loss to infra services, GPU nodes are being marked unhealthy and a few p100s got evicted. APM spikes in 10.2s window. Anyone else seeing this?

maria-nguyen: seeing same. model-serving latency for heavy-chat queue up ~3-4x. Autoscaler started scaling down then back up, causing eviction churn. :frowning:

samir: alerted. checking node pool events now. `kubectl get nodes --selector=gpu=true -o wide` shows 6 nodes NotReady with `NetworkPluginFailed`.

kevin: cloud provider status shows "Interconnect degraded" for eu-west2 https://status.cloudprovider.example/incident/789

lisa: KMS calls are timing out for objects in eu-west2, getting 503 on key unwrap. This is blocking Private deployments that have KMS in same region.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0456 — GCP interconnect degradation eu-west2. Severity: Sev 2. Assigned: oncall-infra

oncall-infra: I'm on it. First goal: stop further node churn and keep customer traffic alive. Suggestions: 1) disable scale-in on gpu-autoscaler, 2) route traffic to eu-west3 and eu-central for non-sensitive tenants, 3) activate fallback KMS in eu-west1 for Private tenants.

alex_ross: I'm disabling scale-in: `kubectl annotate hpa gpu-hpa autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-in-disabled=true` — will hold for 15m.

maria-nguyen: Starting traffic shift for public traffic: update traffic router policy to prefer eu-west3 if latency < 250ms and eu-west2 health != healthy. Rolling out canary to 10% now. :gear:

samir: For KMS fallback, we have a hermetic flow: if kms-unwrap fails after 3 retries, switch keyring env var to `eu-west1-fallback` and continue. Deploying a patch to bypass strict region affinity for 1 hour. Pushing config change to private-control-plane.

kevin: Contacted cloud provider support; they confirm fiber provider has a flap and are rerouting; ETA 1-2 hours. No immediate ETA on eviction stabilization.

lisa: To reduce memory pressure and avoid further evictions, we're hot-switching some heavy models to quantized variants (int8) for the affected pools. This reduces GPU memory ~30% and should keep more pods alive.

oncall-infra: Good. Also enabling prefix KV cache to reduce token load: set `CACHE_PREFIX=true` on serving-config for heavy-chat route.

ops-bot: Alert: Cost anomaly detected — cross-region egress spike anticipated due to traffic shifting. Estimated +$3.2k/hr if sustained.

alex_ross: We accept the cost for the next 2 hours to maintain availability. Finance: FYI — we may need to pull from incident budget. @kevin please log cost breakdown later.

samir: Rolling restart of affected gpu node pool with `gcloud compute instances reset` not recommended; provider may reassign. We're instead cordoning nodes: `kubectl drain` then let managed instance group recreate in stable zones.

maria-nguyen: Canary passed @10%. Incrementing to 40% now. No errors in logs apart from transient KMS timeouts which are now served by fallback.

kevin: Cloud-support-bot: Support case 12345 updated — provider re-routed traffic, packet loss reduced to 1.2%. They will keep monitoring. Next update in 30m.

lisa: Evictions stopped after quantized switch and scale-in disabled. Monitoring GPU utilization — down from 92% to 64% on avg.

oncall-infra: We'll keep the temporary flags for 90m, then revert scale-in annotation and rollback kms fallback if provider confirms stable. Postmortem owner: lisa. Action items:
- collect kube events (samir)
- cost runbook (kevin)
- eval quantized perf regression (maria-nguyen)
- provider comms (alex_ross)

alex_ross: Thanks team. Adding incident notes to #postmortems after stabilization. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0456 status -> mitigated. Will transition to monitoring state.
